question: If $P = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, show that $P$ is its own inverse. Also, calculate $P^3$.
explanation:
To show $P$ is its own inverse, we must show $PP=I$.

$PP = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0\times0 + 1\times1 & 0\times1+1\times0 \\ 1\times0+0\times1 & 1\times1+0\times0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Hence, $P^{-1}=P$.

Now, $P^3 = P \cdot P \cdot P = I \cdot P = P$.
